chunks: From him, from al-Abbas, from one of our companions, who said:

I wrote to him: 'May I be your ransom. A woman bequeathed to another woman and gave her five hundred dirhams. She had a husband and children. She instructed her to give a share from it to some of her daughters and to devote the remainder to the Imam.' He wrote back: 'One-third of that is to be given to me, and the remainder is to be distributed among the heirs according to the shares of Allah (i.e., the divine shares of inheritance).'

key_terms.سِهَامِ اللَّهِ: Shares of Allah (referring to the Imam's share in khums or specific inheritance portions)

ai.seo_question: How is an estate distributed when the deceased leaves specific bequests alongside standard heirs like a husband and children?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the distribution of the deceased's estate by distinguishing between the Imam's specific share (one-third) and the residual portion allocated to heirs according to the 'shares of God' (sahm Allah). It highlights the Shia jurisprudential view on the Imam's right to a portion of the estate in the absence of specific bequests to non-heirs, while ensuring the remaining assets are divided among the surviving husband and children.
